column2: To hold a work as one's own is to acknowledge oneself as its author inwardly and, wherever one speaks of it, in speech as well, neither disowning it nor laying it on another in either.
Acknowledging a work of one's own is holding it as one's own and naming it for what it is.

The deeds a work of one's own rightly calls for are those that answer, in proportion, what it did that is not yet answered, to those it touched or in one's own conduct, and those that carry its good or its lesson to others; a deed that cannot be done, or that would shift onto the innocent a cost that is one's own to bear, is not called for.
